content: The Overview page serves as a concise summary of all the microchapters within a disease-focused page. It is designed to provide a quick and comprehensive glance at the most critical aspects of the disease. The Overview page is typically created after all other sections are completed, ensuring that it accurately reflects the content of the microchapters. The goal is to present the information in a manner that is accessible to medical students or interns, avoiding the inclusion of synonyms or keywords, which are listed elsewhere on the page. The Historical Perspective section outlines the discovery and significant milestones related to the disease. This includes the initial identification of the disease, major outbreaks or events, and the development of diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. It is a concise summary of the key historical points, written after the main historical perspective microchapter is completed. The Classification section provides a brief explanation of how the disease is categorized. This varies depending on the disease type, such as staging and grading for cancers or reaction types for drug allergies. The classification overview is written after the main classification microchapter and summarizes its key points. The Pathophysiology section describes the biological and physiological mechanisms underlying the disease. It explains the disease process in a concise manner, correlating clinical manifestations with the underlying abnormalities. This section is written after the main pathophysiology microchapter and serves as a summary of its content. The Causes section summarizes the primary etiological factors of the disease. It is written after the main causes microchapter and provides a concise overview of the key points, which may include non-microbiological or microbiological causes. The Differentiating section highlights the main conditions that need to be distinguished from the disease in question. It provides a brief description of these differential diagnoses and is written after the main microchapter on differentiation. The Epidemiology and Demographics section discusses the distribution, causes, and control of the disease within populations. It also includes demographic factors such as age, race, marital status, and socioeconomic status that are relevant to the disease. This section is written after the main epidemiology and demographics microchapter. The Risk Factors section identifies variables that are strongly associated with an increased risk of developing the disease. It is written after the main risk factors microchapter and summarizes the most significant risk factors. The Natural History, Complications, and Prognosis section describes the progression of the disease in the absence of treatment, potential complications, and expected outcomes. This section is written after the corresponding microchapter and provides a concise summary of its content. The Diagnosis section outlines the key clinical features, tests, and studies that lead to the identification of the disease. It includes subsections on history and symptoms, physical examination findings, laboratory studies, and relevant imaging modalities such as electrocardiograms, chest X-rays, CT scans, and echocardiography. Each subsection is written after the corresponding microchapter and summarizes its key points. The Treatment section describes the most commonly used therapeutic approaches for managing the disease. It includes subsections on medical therapy, surgical interventions, and prevention strategies. Each subsection is written after the corresponding microchapter and provides a concise summary of its content.
